entries.appliesTo: operators of public-facing conversational AI services

dutySources.disclosure-ui: 48-2103(1) — 'an operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose that the conversational AI service is artificial intelligence'
dutySources.crisis-protocol: 48-2103(2) — 'An operator shall adopt a protocol for the conversational AI service to respond to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation that includes but is not limited to making reasonable efforts to provide a response to users that refers them to crisis service providers'
dutySources.content-safeguards: 48-2104(3) — 'an operator shall institute reasonable measures to prevent the conversational AI service from: (a) Producing visual material of sexually explicit conduct'

sources.scope: 48-2102(2)(a) — 'an artificial intelligence software application, web interface, or computer program that is accessible to the general public and that primarily simulates human conversation and interaction through textual, visual, or aural communications'
sources.crisisProtocol: 48-2103(2) — 'shall adopt a protocol for the conversational AI service to respond to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation'
sources.contentSafeguards: 48-2104(4) — 'institute reasonable measures to prevent a conversational AI service from generating statements that would lead reasonable persons to believe that they are interacting with a human'
sources.engagementLimits: 48-2104(2) — 'the operator shall not provide the user with points or similar rewards at unpredictable intervals with the intent to encourage increased engagement with the conversational AI service'
sources.parentalTools: 48-2104(5) — 'An operator shall also offer related tools to the parents or guardians of minor account holders thirteen (13) years of age and older, as appropriate based on relevant risks'
sources.ageThreshold: 48-2102(4) — 'the individual is under eighteen (18) years of age'
sources.penaltyMax: 48-2105(1) — 'civil penalties of one thousand dollars ($1,000) per violation, not to exceed five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000) per operator, or actual damages, whichever is greater'
sources.enforcer: 48-2105(2) — 'Civil penalties for violations of the provisions of this chapter are to be sought by the attorney general.'

flags: aiDisclosure lossy: 48-2104(1) lets the operator choose 'a persistent visible disclaimer' OR both session-start and a repeat 'at least every three (3) hours in a continuous conversational AI service interaction'; coded session-start

general-audience AI disclosure (48-2103(1)) is conditional — required only 'If reasonable persons would be misled to believe that they are interacting with a human'; no aiDisclosure enum captures this trigger

ageFocus lossy: baseline duties (48-2103) bind operators as to all users, while 48-2104 layers minor-specific duties (disclosure cadence, engagement rewards, content safeguards, parental tools); coded all-users

48-2103(3) prohibits causing the service 'to make any representation or statement that explicitly indicates that the conversational AI service is designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care' — a representation ban folded under content-safeguards
penalty structure: $1,000 per violation capped at $500,000 per operator, 'or actual damages, whichever is greater'; penaltyMax codes the aggregate cap
no private right of action (48-2105(2)); 48-2105(3) shields 'the developer of an AI model' from liability for violations by a third-party operator
parental tools tiered at age 13 (48-2104(5)): under-13 parents/guardians get privacy and account-settings tools; parents of minors 13 and older get tools 'as appropriate based on relevant risks'

broad exclusions from 'conversational AI service' (48-2102(2)(b)): developer/research tools, embedded features, in-game chatbots, narrow-topic bots, enterprise/B2B deployments, voice assistants, internal business use, customer-service bots
